source.text: At least one of the "sub" and "iss" claims MUST be present in the JWT.
However, in the absence of such requirements, all confirmation members that are not understood by implementations MUST be ignored.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: The "cnf" claim value MUST represent only a single proof-of- possession key; thus, at most one of the "jwk", "jwe", and "jku" (JWK Set URL) confirmation values defined below may be present.

source.section_title: Representation of an Asymmetric Proof-of-Possession Key
source.text: The JWK MUST contain the required key members for a JWK of that key type and MAY contain other JWK members, including the "kid" (Key ID) member.

notes: multiple keywords in one sentence; split into one requirement each

source.section_title: Representation of an Asymmetric Proof-of-Possession Key
source.text: The "jwk" member MAY also be used for a JWK representing a symmetric key, provided that the JWT is encrypted so that the key is not revealed to unintended parties.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.section_title: Representation of an Asymmetric Proof-of-Possession Key
source.text: If the JWT is not encrypted, the symmetric key MUST be encrypted as described below.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.section_title: Representation of a URL for a Proof-of-Possession Key
source.text: If there are multiple keys in the referenced JWK Set document, a "kid" member MUST also be included with the referenced key's JWK also containing the same "kid" value.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.section_title: Representation of a URL for a Proof-of-Possession Key
source.text: The protocol used to acquire the resource MUST provide integrity protection.

source.section_title: Representation of a URL for a Proof-of-Possession Key
source.text: An HTTP GET request to retrieve the JWK Set MUST use TLS [RFC5246] and the identity of the server MUST be validated, as per Section 6 of RFC 6125 [RFC6125].

Because a core goal of this specification is for the resulting representations to be compact, it is RECOMMENDED that the name be short -- not to exceed eight characters without a compelling reason to do so.
